previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted after undergoing radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for a liver tumor. He presented with post-procedural hypotension and lethargy, initially attributed to pain medications. During his hospitalization, he developed a right hemothorax, which was managed with chest tube drainage. He also experienced intermittent fevers, but cultures from blood, urine, and ascitic fluid showed no infection, suggesting a post-procedural inflammatory cause. His condition improved with supportive care, including fluid management, pain control, and diuretics for ascites. The chest tube was removed without recurrence, and he was transitioned to oral medications. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for chemo-embolization of a second liver lesion and close outpatient follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Pre-procedure chest radiograph.

IMPRESSION: Previously seen mild right pleural effusion since ___
has now completely resolved.  Bibasal atelectasis has also significantly
resolved and now only minimal basal atelectasis is persisting.  There is no
pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  Rest of the lung fields are clear.  There
is mild cardiomegaly.  Cardiomediastinal contours are normal.

CHEMOEMBOLIZATION OF THE LIVER

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ man with cirrhosis and hepatocellular
carcinoma status post radiofrequency ablation, for second lesion selective
hepatocellular carcinoma chemoembolization.

PHYSICIANS:  Dr. ___, the attending radiologist, and Dr. ___
___, fellow.

PROCEDURES:
1.  Selective superior mesenteric artery arteriogram.
2.  Selective celiac arteriogram.
3.  Selective catheterization of the third-order branch of the left hepatic
artery and rotational angiography with Dyna CT reconstruction.
4.  Right external iliac artery sheath injection.
5.  Selective chemoembolization of hypervascular lesion in the segment II of
the left hepatic lobe.

INTRAVENOUS MEDICATIONS ADMINISTERED DURING THE PROCEDURE:  The procedure was
performed under monitored conscious sedation.  The patient received a total
quantity of 75 mcg of fentanyl and 1.5 mg of Versed during the total
procedural time of 115 minutes, while his hemodynamic parameters and pulse
oximetry were continuously monitored by a trained radiology nurse.

INTRA-ARTERIAL MEDICATIONS ADMINISTERED DURING THE PROCEDURE:  50 mg of
doxorubicin, 10 mL lipiodol, 15 mL of 1% lidocaine.

Informed consent for the procedure was obtained from the patient via
professional interpreter after risks and potential complications of the
procedure had been explained.  The skin of the right inguinal region was
prepped and draped in sterile fashion.  Usual timeout and huddle protocols
were carried out prior to the procedure according to the ___
policy.  Under fluoroscopic guidance and palpation, right common femoral
artery was localized superficial to the anatomical landmark of the right
femoral head.  Local anesthesia was affected by 1% lidocaine.  Right common
femoral artery was accessed using a single wall micropuncture technique,
utilizing 21-gauge needle.  A 5 ___ sheath was advanced into the right
common femoral artery over 0.035 ___ guidewire.  A 5 ___ ___
catheter was then advanced into the aortic arch and formed followed by
selective catheterization of the superior mesenteric artery and of the celiac
artery, respectively.

Renegade ___ microcatheter was advanced through the ___ catheter
successfully into the left hepatic artery and then further advanced under
direct fluoroscopic guidance using roadmapping into the third-order branch of
the left hepatic artery supplying the target lesion.  A Transcend wire and
double-angle microglide wire were used in conjunction with Renegade
microcatheter.  Once location of the microcatheter was documented by ___ to
provide the blood supply for the targeted lesion, chemoembolization was
successfully delivered under continued fluoroscopic visualization.

Manual compression was applied to hemostasis.

FINDINGS:  
1.  Selective superior mesenteric artery arteriogram demonstrated a replaced
right hepatic artery.  Superior mesenteric artery demonstrated normal luminal
contour without stenosis. Portal vein was widely patent on superior mesenteric
artery arteriogram. A large laminated gallstone is demonstrated incidentally
in the gallbladder.
2.  No arterial enhancing areas were seen in the right lobe, particularly in
the area treated previously with RF ablation.
3.  Selective injection of the celiac trunk demonstrated a replaced left
hepatic artery originating from the left gastric artery.
4.  Injection of the celiac trunk demonstrated a vascular blush in the left
hepatic lobe in the segment II corresponding to the targeted lesion. 
Successful targeted chemoembolization was performed.

CONCLUSION:  Successful selective chemoembolization of the hypervascular
lesion in the segment II of the left hepatic lobe.

INDICATION:  ___ man with TACE on ___.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___, CT of the abdomen and
pelvis from ___ and chemoembolization of the liver from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired through the abdomen without IV contrast.
Multiplanar reformations were obtained and reviewed.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:

The partially imaged lungs show a small nonhemorrhagic right effusion.  The
left lung is clear.  The heart is unremarkable.  Gynecomastia is partially
imaged.  

Evaluation of the solid organs is limited due to the lack of IV contrast.  

Within these limitations, the abdomen shows high-density Ethiodol contrast in
the segment II and III of the left lobe of the liver with a more focal,
spherical hyperattenuating area consistent with the known HCC.  No other areas
of infiltration by Ethiodol are noted.  A right segment VII lesion, which was
previously ablated, is essentially unchanged compared to the prior
examination. Liver is shrunken and cirrhotic and multiple splenic varices are
consistent with known cirrhosis.  

The gallbladder with large stones within it is unchanged.  The spleen, both
adrenals, both kidneys and pancreas are unremarkable.  Mild mesenteric
stranding is noted diffusely through the abdomen, unchanged.  The small and
large bowel loops are unremarkable.  No abdominal, retroperitoneal or
mesenteric lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria is present.  Trace simple free
fluid is noted.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:

The visible osseous structures show multilevel degenerative disease with
endplate changes in the lower thoracic and upper lumbar spine, unchanged.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Ethiodol contrast noted in segment II and III of the liver.  No other
areas of unexpected Ethiodol infiltration noted.  

2.  Small nonhemorrhagic right pleural effusion.

INDICATION FOR STUDY:  History of cirrhosis, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy,
presents with new onset headache.  Study is to evaluate for possible
intracranial hemorrhage.

COMPARISON EXAM:  There are no comparison exams available.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT-acquired axial images from the level of C1 to the
vertex were obtained through the brain.  Axial images were displayed with 5-mm
slice thickness.  No IV contrast was administered for the study.

CT OF HEAD WITHOUT CONTRAST:
There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, masses, mass effect or infarction. 
Ventricles and sulci are normal in caliber and configuration.  No fractures
are identified.

IMPRESSION: Normal study.
